title: Buy automation only when review-adjusted cost and risk both improve
observed_evidence: 820 deduplicated CUAD outputs contain 38 errors. Contract-grouped retrospective validation yields mean trained lift 8.45 versus raw lift 0.00; this small sample cannot establish production ROI.
executive_recommendation: Prefer a bounded triage evaluation over blanket auto-acceptance. Measure exception-review time and error exposure at contract level before paying fixed integration costs.
priorities: Block auto-acceptance when no simultaneous risk bound is feasible.
Compare review-all and calibrated triage at the same contract workload, including QA and integration costs.
Expand automation only if observed review time and residual error stay below the predeclared gates.
reversal: Review-all wins at low volume or if exception review consumes the apparent savings; no option should ship if the risk ceiling fails.
uncertainty: Clause correctness is not legal-loss severity; assumed incident rates and dollar losses are not estimates from the 38 errors.

economics.evidence_status: ILLUSTRATIVE ASSUMPTIONS, NOT MEASURED COSTS OR RISK

product.randomization_unit: reviewer account (contract team clusters in a real trial)
product.incident_definition: material error in an exported review
product.retention_interpretation: reviewer performs another eligible contract review
